chunks: As for what Saʿd narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-ʿAbbās ibn Maʿrūf, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muskān, from al-Ḥasan ibn al-Sirrī, from ʿUmar ibn Yazīd, who said:
I said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: May a man recite the same surah in the two rakʿahs of the obligatory prayer? He said: There is no harm, if it is more than three verses.

The proper way concerning this report is that we understand it to mean that it is permissible for him to repeat it in the second rakʿah without dividing it, and that is when he does not recite well any other than it. But if he recites other than it well, then that is disliked. That which indicates this is as follows.

key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: the two rakʿahs of the prayer
key_terms.ثَلَاثِ آيَاتٍ: three verses, used here as a minimum threshold
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to recite the same surah in both rakʿahs of an obligatory prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of repeating the same surah in both rakʿahs of an obligatory prayer. It states that there is no harm in doing so when the surah is more than three verses, and the accompanying explanation restricts this permissibility to a case where the person does not properly know another surah, while otherwise considering it disliked.
